lines.li: [them] Is the one of ours in your cells eating?
[us] The same as we do.
[them,their:tribal] Then tell them their people haven't forgotten them.
[them] Then I can tell their family that much, at least.
[them] Among my people a captive is traded back for goods, never for silver.
[us] Then your people should say what goods.
[them] They will, when the elders are ready.
[them] My lord will pay for the one you hold, if your price is honest.
[us] It's your people who name the price, not us.
[them] Then I hope they name an honest one.
[them] My people will make an offer for the one you're holding, through the proper channels.
[us] We'll be listening.
[them,their:spacer] Good, and do keep a record of their condition.
[them] Good, and try not to let the price go up while we wait.
[them] You've got one of ours behind a locked door.
[us] And they'll be fed while they're there.
[them] Fed isn't free.
[them] It's hard to be friendly with one of mine in your cells.
[us] Then don't be friendly, just be civil.
[them] I hear your colony keeps prisoners.
[us] A few, and they're fed.
[them] Anyone my people would want back?
[us] Not that I know of.
[us] What do your people do when one of their own is taken?
[them,their:tribal] We trade goods for them, or we go and take them back.
[them,their:medieval] We send a messenger with a purse and hope the price is honest.
[them,their:industrial] We get on the radio and start haggling.
[them,their:empire] The Empire pays in silver, and remembers who set the price.
[them,their:spacer] We open negotiations and keep a record of every offer made.
[them] We pay if we can, and we remember who held them.
[us] We'd do much the same.
[us] Your people are holding one of ours, and I want them home.
[them] I'd want the same, in your place.
[them,their:tribal] I'll carry your words to the elders myself.
[them] I'll say so at home, though it isn't mine to decide.
[them] You hold one of ours, and we hold one of yours.
[us] Then there's a trade to be made.
[them,their:lowtech] One for one at the gate is the old way, and a good one.
[them] There may be, if both sides are sensible about it.
[them] My people will want silver for the one of yours they hold, I expect.
[us] We'll pay what's fair.
[them] Fair is a big word in that kind of bargain.
[them] The one of yours we hold is held with honor, as the court requires.
[us] We only want them back.
[them] Then your colony knows how such things are settled.
[us] One of ours is still in your people's hands.
[them] Then you'd better be civil to me.
[us] You've seen the inside of our cells at {CAPTOR}, I hear.
[them] I have, and I prefer this side of the gate.
[us] So do we, for you.
[them] My people bargained to have me back from {CAPTOR}.
[us] And here you are.
[them,their:tribal] Worth whatever they gave for me, I keep telling them.
[them] Walking in by the gate I walked out of, which still feels strange.
[them] I don't hold my time at {CAPTOR} against your people.
[us] That's generous.
[them] You fed me and let me go home, and plenty wouldn't have.
[them] I spent days in your cells at {CAPTOR}, so forgive me if I don't smile.
[us] Fair enough.
[them] My children still ask me what it was like at {CAPTOR}.
[us] What do you tell them?
[them] That the walls were thick, the food was plain, and I came home.
[them] Your warden walked me out of {CAPTOR} as if I were a guest leaving.
[us] By then you nearly were.
[them] That's how I tell it at home.
[them] The last bargain over captives between our peoples was settled fairly, I'm told.
[us] It was.
[them,their:tribal] Then the goods and the captive both went where they should.
[them] Then there's no bad blood over it, as far as I'm concerned.
[them] Your colony let one of ours walk home and asked nothing for it.
[us] Keeping them wasn't doing anyone any good.
[them,their:lowtech] Among us a gift like that is answered, sooner or later.
[them] My people are still working out what to make of it.
[them] One of my people went into your cells and never came out.
[us] We didn't want that.
